findings.section: Root cause / Claims vs findings (cache-key row)
findings.problem: The report states 'the server pays the full-window cost per appended event, back-to-back' and marks 'every appended event invalidates the entry and an active thread rebuilds continuously' as Verified. The cache-key part is true, but the client deliberately paces its trailing refetch to the observed fetch duration (min 50 ms, max 1 s, ~50% duty cycle) and coalesces events that arrive mid-fetch, so builds are NOT once-per-appended-event; PR #882 introduced exactly this pacing. The sustained-rebuild mechanism is real but its magnitude is overstated.
findings.evidence: apps/app/src/hooks/cache-owners/realtime-cache-registry.ts L135-L157 at 16ceb3a54: 'Waiting out the observed build cost caps that duty cycle near 50%'; TRAILING_REFETCH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 50, resolveTrailingRefetchDelayMs(observedFetchDurationMs). PR #882 body: 'The client's trailing refetch is paced to the observed build duration.'
findings.fix: Reword the row to 'Verified (cache key) / Partially: the client throttles refetches to ~50% duty cycle, so rebuilds are sustained but coalesced, not one per event' and cite realtime-cache-registry.ts.

findings.problem: The first `it(...)` is titled 'a full 1500-event window builds within the documented ~100ms cold-build target' but never asserts that (only `expect(samples.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`; full-window n=0 in both runs). A reader running vitest sees a passing test whose name promises a check that is not made.
findings.evidence: timeline-event-budget-cost.repro.test.ts L87, L174, output line 'full-window builds (>= 1350 events, n=0)'.
findings.fix: Rename the first scenario to something like 'per-event cost across the perf fixture (informational)'.

findings.section: Root cause — Deeper issue / Related issues
findings.problem: The report presents 'the budget bounds count, not bytes' as its own discovered deeper issue, but PR #882's own 'Known limits' already states 'The budget bounds event count, not bytes' and '1500 is a first guess ... The new logs are how we'll tune it'. Not crediting this makes the calibration gap look unanticipated when the original author flagged it.
findings.evidence: gh pr view 882 body, 'Known limits' section.
findings.fix: Add one sentence in Related issues / Deeper issue noting PR #882 already listed the count-vs-bytes limitation and called 1500 a first guess.

findings.problem: The contended run is a synthetic slowdown whose pass/fail depends on the host: the threshold is 100 ms and measured p50 was 124.5 ms (author) / 141.9 ms (me); on a faster CPU sharing one core with three busy loops it could pass. run-contended.sh also hardcodes CORE=3 and requires `taskset` (Linux only) without saying so in the report body.
findings.evidence: run-contended.sh (CORE=${CORE:-3}, taskset), verify output p50=141.9 vs 124.5.
findings.fix: State the Linux/taskset prerequisite and that the assertion is expected to fail only when the throttled per-event cost exceeds ~0.067 ms; optionally use 4-5 busy loops for margin.
